react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis tools converge on Tryptophan metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this differential metabolite set. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism as the top hit with FDR = 8.86×10⁻¹⁹, fold enrichment 875.7, and 7 of 9 input metabolites overlapping the pathway roster. MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00380 at p = 5.41×10⁻⁹ with the same six serotonin-path branch members. Mummichog m/z-direct activity ranked the same network first (p = 8.40×10⁻⁵) with 16 of 17 empirical-compound nodes matched to input metabolites. Reactome R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) appeared as rank 7 in RaMP with 3 confirmed members (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, FDR = 2.02×10⁻⁸). The seven overlapping metabolites span the full kynurenine-to-NAD⁺ branch (L-tryptophan → 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid → quinolinic acid) and the serotonin-melatonin branch (L-tryptophan → tryptamine → serotonin → melatonin), with indoleacetaldehyde as the shared aldehyde intermediate. N-carbamoyl-L-aspartic acid (ureidosuccinic acid) and O-phosphoethanolamine were not captured by the tryptophan network and appear in RaMP as weak hits in pyrimidine and glycerophospholipid metabolism respectively; they may reflect treatment-specific off-pathway perturbations. The cross-paradigm consensus strongly implicates tryptophan catabolism as the biological process most sensitive to the treatment.
